summary: Marcelle Lalou was a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She studied at the University of Paris and EPHE under Sylvain Lévi, Jean Przyluski, Jacques Bacot, and Paul Pelliot, later teaching at EPHE (1938–1963) and editing Journal Asiatique (1950–1966).
Marco Ferrante works in the fields of Indology and philosophy. He has held posts at the University of Rome (attested 2014) and the Austrian Academy of Sciences.
Marco Walther is a Tibetologist. He completed his PhD at the University of Munich (attested 2017) under the supervision of Franz-Karl Ehrhard and also studied under Khenpo Dondrub Namgyal.

Marcus Bingenheimer specializes in Buddhist studies and Sinology. Educated at Nagoya, Heidelberg, and the University of Würzburg under Norbert Klaes, he held positions at the Dharma Drum Institute (2005–2011), Chung-Hwa Institute (~2005–2008), and Temple University (2012–2015).

Marek Mejor is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology. He held a Junior Research Fellowship at Wolfson College, Oxford (1981–1982) and served as a professor at the University of Warsaw (attested 2000–2010).

Marek Zemánek specializes in religious studies and Buddhist studies. He studied at Dongguk University, Seoul National University, and the University of Prague, completing his dissertation under Radek Chlup.
Marek Zvelebil was an archaeologist and historian. He studied at the University of Sheffield, where he later held an academic post from circa 1981 until 2011.
Margaret Cone is a scholar in Indology, Buddhist studies, and linguistics. She held posts at the University of Cambridge and Darwin College, Cambridge (both attested 1996).

Margaret Dornish worked in religious studies and Sinology. She studied at the University of Southern California, Claremont Graduate University, and Yale University, later serving as Associate Professor of Religion at Pomona College (attested 1989).
Margaret Gouin specializes in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. She earned her PhD at the University of Bristol under the supervision of Paul Williams.

Margaret J. Pearson works in Sinology and history/archaeology. She pursued doctoral studies at the University of Washington under Hellmut Wilhelm and Burton Watson, and served as a Visiting Fellow at Clare Hall, Cambridge in 1997.

Margaret Mead studied at Barnard and Columbia under Franz Boas. She held long-term posts at the American Museum of Natural History (1926; 1946–1969) and Columbia University (1954–1978), alongside positions at Fordham, The New School, and the University of Rhode Island.

Margaret R. Miles is a religious studies scholar and historian. After studying at SFSU and the Graduate Theological Union, she taught at Harvard Divinity School (~1978–1996) and served as dean at the Graduate Theological Union (1996–2001).

Margarita Angelica Delgado Creamer is a scholar of religious studies, Japanology, and Buddhist studies. She earned her PhD from the University of Pittsburgh under Linda Penkower (attested 2016) and completed postdoctoral training with Xiuping Hong.

Margarita Iosifovna Vorobyova-Desyatovskaya was a scholar of Buddhist, Indological, and Iranian/Central Asian studies. Educated at the University of Saint Petersburg, she worked at the Institute of Oriental Studies (~1956–2021) and the Institute of Oriental Manuscripts (1982–2005).
Margarita Kleibel is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She studied under Karin Preisendanz as well as Klaus-Dieter Mathes, who served as her MA supervisor (attested 2010).

Maria Heim is a scholar of Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Indology. She studied at Reed College and earned her PhD at Harvard under Charles Hallisey, later serving as an associate professor at Amherst College (attested 2013–2020).

Marian Ury specialized in Japanology and Buddhist studies. She earned her PhD from the University of California, Berkeley (circa 1965) and served as a professor of East Asian languages and comparative literature at UC Davis (1969–1995).

Marianne Pieper studied at the University of Hamburg and completed her habilitation at Magdeburg in 1996. She held teaching appointments at Kassel (1994–1996) and Hamburg, where she served as professor of sociology from 1996 to 2015.

Marianne Winder specialized in Tibetology and Buddhist studies, studying at the University of London, Nottingham, UCL, and SOAS under David Snellgrove. She held posts at Nottingham and London, later serving as curator and consultant at the Wellcome Trust.
